raw_case_text: A 50-year-old man, with diagnosed alcoholic cirrhosis for the past decade, abstaining from alcohol since then, with no history of any cirrhotic complications, under no supportive treatment apart for regular follow-up, was admitted for protracted fever of two months' duration, accompanied by low backache, mild diarrhea, and abdominal distention. He had a history of splenectomy and was a shepherd. Significant ascites, accompanied by moderate pleural fluid effusion, was noted on clinical examination and subsequent imaging, the latter also demonstrating abdominal lymphadenopathy with partial central necrosis. Laboratory tests, compared to his latest follow-up, demonstrated only an increase in CRP and total and direct bilirubin. Blood cultures were positive for B. melitensis, a finding further confirmed by Rose Bengal plate agglutination, Wright seroagglutination test, and ELISA serology (Serion ELISA IgG/IgM/IgA antibodies to Brucella melitensis). The patient was treated with doxycycline 100 mg twice daily, rifampicin 600 mg daily, and ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily. Defervescence was achieved on day 5, accompanied though by progressive worsening of liver biochemistry indices and mild prolongation of international normalized ratio (INR) to levels of 1.34 (nv 0.8-1.2). Rifampicin dose was halved, and diuretics were added to treat ascites. Despite improvement/stabilization of other biochemical indices in later days, serum bilirubin continued to increase, reaching a plateau of total 7.2 mg/dl/direct 4.2 mg/dl and the patient was discharged, continuing treatment and follow-up as an outpatient on day 16. On day 41, the patient was readmitted with hepatic encephalopathy and jaundice. Hepatic biochemistry was steady, but total bilirubin was 16.7 mg/dl (direct bilirubin 13.6 mg/dl) and INR was 1.44. Ascites was minimal and subsequent workup excluded any underlying causes of encephalopathy. Antibiotics were discontinued as potential inducers of severe hepatotoxicity, and the patient was referred to a transplantation center due to the gradual worsening of liver function indices. He underwent liver transplantation which unfortunately had an adverse postoperative outcome.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 50-year-old male with alcoholic cirrhosis presented with protracted fever of two months' duration, low backache, mild diarrhea, and abdominal distention.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient had a 10-year history of alcoholic cirrhosis (abstinent since diagnosis) without prior decompensation. He presented with a 2-month history of protracted fever accompanied by low backache, mild diarrhea, and progressive abdominal distention. During hospitalization, defervescence was achieved on day 5 of therapy, but he developed progressive worsening of liver function and was discharged on day 16. On day 41, he was readmitted with hepatic encephalopathy and severe jaundice.
subjective.past_medical_history: Alcoholic cirrhosis diagnosed 10 years prior (abstinent since diagnosis, no history of cirrhotic complications, no supportive medications); status post splenectomy. Epidemiological exposure/Occupation: Shepherd.
subjective.review_of_systems: Low backache and mild diarrhea. Home medications: None (regular follow-up only). Allergies: None documented.

objective.physical_examination: Admission: Significant ascites and moderate pleural fluid effusion. Readmission (day 41): Hepatic encephalopathy, marked jaundice, and minimal ascites.
objective.routine_investigations: Baseline labs: Elevated CRP and increased total and direct bilirubin compared to baseline follow-up. Day 5: Progressive worsening of liver biochemistry and mild prolongation of international normalized ratio (INR) to 1.34 (normal values 0.8-1.2). Day 16: Total serum bilirubin plateaued at 7.2 mg/dl with direct bilirubin 4.2 mg/dl. Day 41 readmission: Total bilirubin 16.7 mg/dl, direct bilirubin 13.6 mg/dl, INR 1.44, with steady hepatic biochemistry.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal imaging: Significant ascites, moderate pleural effusion, and abdominal lymphadenopathy with partial central necrosis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Brucellosis confirmed by blood cultures positive for Brucella melitensis, further verified by Rose Bengal plate agglutination test, Wright seroagglutination test, and Serion ELISA serology (IgG/IgM/IgA antibodies to Brucella melitensis). Underlying causes of encephalopathy excluded on repeat workup.
Plan & Clinical Course: Initiated on doxycycline 100 mg twice daily, rifampicin 600 mg daily, and ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily. Defervescence achieved on day 5 but accompanied by progressive liver function impairment and coagulopathy (INR 1.34); rifampicin dose was halved and diuretics added for ascites. Discharged on day 16. Readmitted on day 41 with hepatic encephalopathy and severe hyperbilirubinemia (total bilirubin 16.7 mg/dl, direct 13.6 mg/dl, INR 1.44). Antibiotics were discontinued due to hepatotoxicity, and the patient was referred for emergency liver transplantation, which had an adverse postoperative outcome.
